title: MIDWATER ANIMALS
description: Animals suspended in the water column. Many are gelatinous; some produce bioluminescent signals.

entries.name: Atolla jellies
entries.note: Bell pulses and trailing tentacles; prototype glow is artistic.

title: SEAFLOOR ANIMALS
description: Mobile animals living on or near the bottom. These are not automatically heat-loving extremophiles.

entries.name: Dumbo octopuses
entries.note: Fin-assisted swimming; species occupy different depth ranges.

entries.name: Giant isopods
entries.note: Crustacean scavengers; geographic range and depth vary by species.

title: COLD-WATER HABITAT BUILDERS
description: Corals and sponges provide structure on suitable cooler substrates, away from hot vent discharge.

entries.name: Deep-sea corals and sponges
entries.note: Authored branching/cup forms, not identified species or photo-derived skins.

title: VENT ANIMALS AND SYMBIOSIS
description: Animals around mixed vent waters may rely on microbial partners. They do not live in undiluted superheated fluid.

entries.name: Giant tubeworm · Riftia pachyptila
entries.note: Internal chemosynthetic bacterial partners support nutrition.

entries.name: Vent crustaceans
entries.note: Small animated forms add activity; not identified or anatomically accurate shrimp.

title: BACTERIA AND ARCHAEA
description: Microbial life includes chemosynthetic communities. Metabolism and tolerance are different characteristics.

entries.name: Chimney microbial communities
entries.note: Old City chimney samples show varied cell shapes. Pale scenery mats are illustrative; the photograph does not identify a species by shape.

title: EXTREMOPHILE RESEARCH TARGETS
description: Organize adaptations independently: high pressure (piezophily), high temperature (thermophily), high pH (alkaliphily), and others. Tolerating a condition is not necessarily preferring it.

entries.name: Pressure-adapted microbes
entries.note: Select a documented species and culture evidence before implementing research rewards.
